H_hierarchical.evidence: The MRASM sample is represented as a flat ST0-ST9 transition-link table; the paper describes layers/modules but no parent state with child substates.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Beyond single qualifier rows in Table I, the controller uses nested/composed guards such as motion detected plus insufficient light, wrong code with three allowed checks, exit with count nonzero, and min/max water-level checks.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: Transitions and algorithms include relay actuation, pump/AC/light/door control, buzzer, SMS/message sending, LCD display, access grant/deny, and increment/decrement of occupancy count.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: Dedicated abnormal/security branches exist: abnormal sensor condition sends SMS and takes corrective action; wrong password after three trials triggers alarm/message, but no global any-state safe escape is specified.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State/qualifier/output rows are in Table I, relay-to-device meanings are in the following design prose, and counter/password/alarm semantics appear later in Algorithm I and the demonstration section.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as tamper-proof, abnormal condition, corrective action, and security threat imply security/fault handling semantics not fully formalized as transitions.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: The explicit state table lists relay/output columns, while actions such as pump turns on, AC turns on, alarm/message/display, and occupancy count updates are described narratively elsewhere.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The room-light logic combines entrance/motion with darkness and count checks; keypad logic combines incorrect code with a three-try limit.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: No composite parent state with entry/during/exit behavior is defined; the ST0-ST9 MRASM chart is flat.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: The paper does not declare a from-any-state fault transition or global safe-state escape rule.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: No composite-state initialization or pseudo-chain is present.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: Several guards involve nested boolean/numeric conditions: entrance and dark, exit and count, wrong password and three attempts, and water minimum/maximum thresholds.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: The controller is set ON and runs a continuous monitoring loop over keypad, smoke, temperature, room light, and water; the paper says AC, lights, pumps, and other processes are continuously monitored and API communication is triggered at each instance.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Some outputs are abstract or channel-decoupled, such as send message, notify end-user, display dashboard/sink status, but many actions are concrete relay commands.

key_nl_quotes: Whenever any of the qualifiers changes its state, either from logic 1 to logic 0 or from logic 0 to logic 1; there is an event at the output interface.
When motion is detected and there is insufficient light, the signal from this module changes from logic 0 to 1, L13-L14, the relay known as RL3 is energized and the light turns on.
one_line_pitch: A flat but dense EFSM whose guards, relay actions, notifications, counters, and security/fault branches are spread across tables, prose, algorithms, and demonstration text makes a strong action-and-guard semantic reconstruction stress test.
rationale: The paper gives an explicit ST0-ST9 MRASM transition table, but the real behavioral semantics require integrating the table with design prose, Algorithm I, Algorithm II, and the demonstration section. It is not hierarchical, yet it strongly stresses guard extraction and action attribution through nested sensor conditions, threshold/count logic, relay outputs, SMS/LCD side effects, and security/fault branches. The pyfcstm advantage is broad because expression checking, continuous-monitor aspects, and abstract action separation all map naturally to the sample.
